newest.name: @aibast-agents-library/procurement-supplier-collaboration
newest.description: Run a utility's source-to-pay cycle for network materials from a synthetic snapshot: requisitions from the maintenance plan, capital projects and stock replenishment with the recommended route (framework direct award, mini-competition or open tender) and eligible supplier shortlist, answers to supplier questions from the published RFQ pack, weighted bid scoring with a ranked recommendation, purchase order acknowledgement and ASN delivery deviations, and the three-way match of purchase order, goods receipt and invoice. The agent never awards, orders, messages a supplier or approves a payment; an authorized person approves every step through future authenticated tools.

newest.name: @aibast-agents-library/grid-asset-maintenance
newest.description: Rank a distribution company's grid assets (power transformers, switchgear, underground cables and overhead lines) by failure probability over 30, 90 and 180 days from a synthetic condition-monitoring snapshot, draft the preventive work order with asset history, materials, long-lead parts and crew pre-assignment, check a completed job's field record before the asset register and fixed asset register are updated, and summarize fleet health with the replacement pipeline and capital needed. The agent never raises a work order, orders parts, assigns a crew or changes a register; an authorized engineer approves every step through future authenticated tools.

newest.name: @aibast-agents-library/tiered-huddle-board
newest.description: Run a hospital's daily tiered huddles from one live board built on a synthetic snapshot: every lane from Tier 1 through the Executive tier with each issue's clock against its tier's target, what is past target and what is waiting on the person asking, an escalation draft that restarts the clock at the next tier's target with the reason the next tier reads first and the people to page by name, the closure check that keeps mitigated items open until the person who raised them confirms the fix held, and the decisions the leadership huddle needs today. The agent never escalates, pages, closes or changes an issue; an authorized person confirms every step through future authenticated tools.

newest.name: @aibast-agents-library/campaign-delivery-optimizer

The agent never books inventory, changes a campaign or placement, or shares anything with an advertiser; the sales lead approves every recommendation through future authenticated tools.

newest.name: @aibast-agents-library/content-launch-clearance

The agent never schedules or publishes a title, changes a contract or submits an approval; the rights team approves every launch through future authenticated tools.

newest.name: @aibast-agents-library/live-event-launch-planner
newest.description: Help live operations, community and marketing teams launch a seasonal in-game event from one plan built on a synthetic snapshot: the launch timeline with every milestone to launch day, the readiness checklist across teams with owners and status, the player announcement with its approval and publishing permission, and a summary of late, missing and blocked work. The agent never publishes an announcement, changes a task, sends a reminder or changes the event; the event owners approve every step through future authenticated tools.

newest.name: @aibast-agents-library/first-time-fix

agent_metrics.name: @aibast-agents-library/customer-sentiment-churn
agent_metrics.display_name: Customer Sentiment and Churn Prediction Agent

agent_upvote_coverage.scope: One canonical mirrored GitHub Discussion per agent. Its native upvoteCount is the preference signal, and GitHub permits one active upvote per signed-in account on that Discussion.

agent_acquisition_coverage.scope: One parallel acquisition Discussion per canonical agent. A native upvote records one signed-in account's declared download, copy, or install acquisition. This is separate from observable CDN and release file-transfer counters.

rows.path: docs/vault/Start Here/How to Use This Vault.md

file_metrics.caveat: Only jsDelivr per-file observations are measurable. raw.githubusercontent.com, GitHub Pages, and direct GitHub downloads do not expose public per-file counters here.

rows.display_name: Customer Sentiment and Churn Prediction Agent

workshops.usage_definition: usage_events is the sum of counted GitHub popular-path page views, jsDelivr workshop file downloads, source-bundle downloads, and public workshop feedback reports. It is an event floor, not users or unique usage. The sources use mixed measurement windows, and one person or action can create multiple events.

views.scope: Observed GitHub popular-path rows only, limited to GitHub's 14-day top-path window; absent workshops are censored, not verified zero. Path-level uniques can repeat across paths.

downloads.scope: Validated jsDelivr observations from the canonical tracked-file ledger. Every file mapped to a workshop contributes once; source bundles are partitioned from non-bundle files. Package totals are not added. Raw GitHub, direct GitHub Pages, and unattributed releases are uncounted.

feedback.scope: Paginated public issues, deduplicated by number/id, excluding pull requests, and requiring the marker at body start, exact schema, and one canonical Solution field.

agent_upvotes.scope: Native upvotes on each primary agent's canonical rating Discussion. This preference signal is separate from usage_events and acquisition Discussions.

sources.name: GitHub Popular Paths API
sources.metric: 14-day workshop path views and path-level uniques; not complete GitHub Pages analytics

sources.name: jsDelivr File Stats
sources.metric: paginated workshop files under /solutions/<slug>/ and legacy bundles at /exports/<slug>-source.zip

sources.name: GitHub Releases API
sources.metric: all-time downloads of <slug>-source.zip assets on the solution-bundles release, accumulated across asset replacements

sources.name: GitHub Issues API
sources.metric: public workshop feedback issues identified by label or feedback marker

sources.name: GitHub Agent Upvote Issues
sources.metric: validated per-agent preference events mapped to canonical workshop primaries; excluded from usage_events

sources.name: registry.json
sources.metric: advertised workshop slugs, display names, and quest URLs

achievements.caveat: Verified achievement points are server-scored from opt-in public GitHub progress claims. Each explicitly claimed achievement has a fixed value: started 5, local-proof 15, draft-builder 20, preview-proven 25, workshop-completed 35, and hard-mode-completed 50, for at most 150 points per workshop. Re-syncing unions achievement IDs without duplicating points. Profiles are public by explicit submission consent. GitHub verification confirms authenticated issue authorship and canonical claim format only; achievement completion remains self-reported and is not independently proven. Verified public achievements remain separate from local self-paced state, repository stars, agent upvotes, downloads, and workshop usage events.

workshops.display_name: Customer Sentiment and Churn Prediction Agent

coverage.scope: Public state=all GitHub issues whose body begins with the achievement progress marker and passes the exact schema, canonical workshop-primary-agent, ordered achievement subset, dependency, source, and public-login checks. Open, closed, and edited claims union by case-insensitive login/workshop/achievement.

workshops.display_name: Customer Sentiment and Churn Prediction Agent

coverage.scope: Public GitHub issues with exact cohort or badge qualification markers. Private Microsoft identity, MSIX, customer, roster, and test-answer data are deliberately excluded. Cohorts count only with cohort-verified; qualifications count only with badge-qualified.

rar.reason: RAR federation is intentionally excluded from AIBAST library counts.

agents.display_name: Customer Sentiment and Churn Prediction Agent

ecosystem.caveat: This snapshot counts only AIBAST library channels. Direct agent fetches are observable jsDelivr events, not people, and raw GitHub or raw.githubusercontent.com transfers remain unobservable.

sources.name: GitHub Traffic API
sources.metric: clones, views, popular paths (clones include this repo's own CI checkouts)

sources.name: jsDelivr CDN
sources.metric: per-file download observations across every tracked repository file, including agents, skills, workshops, installers, documentation, code, and assets

sources.name: GitHub Discussions
sources.metric: canonical per-agent preference and signed-in acquisition ledgers using native upvote counts

sources.name: GitHub Issues
sources.metric: structured public workshop feedback, opt-in achievement progress, cohort delivery, and badge qualification triggers validated from issue bodies and reviewer labels
